name: Chloe Nguyen
presenting_complaint: Severe headache and visual disturbance at 34 weeks pregnant with BP 172/114

medications: Aspirin 100 mg nocte (was recommended, adherence uncertain)
medical_history.social: Primary school teacher. Non-smoker. No alcohol. Planned pregnancy.

validation_criteria.presenting_scenario: A 31-year-old primigravida at 34 weeks gestation presents with a severe frontal headache, flashing lights/blurred vision and epigastric pain since this morning. Her hands and face look swollen. Obs: BP 172/114 (repeated 168/112), HR 98, RR 18, SpO2 98%, afebrile, GCS 15. Hyperreflexia with clonus is noted. She has no prior history of hypertension.
validation_criteria.task: Document your assessment and initial management as the admitting RMO.

subjective: Severe/persistent headache not relieved by simple analgesia
Visual disturbance: blurred vision, flashing lights/scotomata
Epigastric or right upper quadrant pain (hepatic capsule stretch / HELLP)
Rapid swelling of hands/face; nausea and vomiting
Fetal movements and any abdominal pain/PV bleeding (screen for abruption)
Risk factors: primigravida, family history of pre-eclampsia, aspirin prophylaxis adherence
objective: Repeat/confirm severe hypertension (BP 172/114, greater than or equal to 160/110) with an appropriate cuff
Neurological: hyperreflexia and clonus, altered vision — signs of severe disease/impending eclampsia
Assess for oedema (face, hands), epigastric/RUQ tenderness
Urine dipstick and protein:creatinine ratio for proteinuria (supportive but NOT required for diagnosis)
Bloods: FBC (platelets), UEC, LFTs, urate, coagulation, LDH, haemolysis screen (HELLP), group and hold
Fetal assessment: CTG for fetal wellbeing and growth/liquor on ultrasound
assessment: Primary diagnosis: Severe pre-eclampsia with severe-range hypertension and neurological features (imminent eclampsia risk)
Explicitly document that proteinuria is NOT required for the diagnosis when there is new hypertension plus end-organ involvement (neurological/hepatic)
Screen for and consider HELLP syndrome given epigastric pain
Differentials considered: gestational hypertension, chronic hypertension, secondary hypertension — but end-organ signs make severe pre-eclampsia the working diagnosis
Recognise definitive treatment is delivery; stabilise mother first
plan: Urgently treat severe hypertension (BP greater than or equal to 160/110): IV labetalol OR oral immediate-release nifedipine OR IV hydralazine, titrated to target BP ~140-155/90-105
Magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis: 4 g IV loading dose over 20 min then 1 g/hour infusion; monitor reflexes, RR and urine output for toxicity (calcium gluconate available as antidote)
Urgent senior obstetric and involve anaesthetics; notify neonatal/paediatric team given 34 weeks
Antenatal corticosteroids (betamethasone) for fetal lung maturity given prematurity
Continuous CTG monitoring, strict fluid balance (avoid fluid overload), IDC for urine output
Full pre-eclampsia bloods and monitor for HELLP; regular BP and neuro observations
Plan for timing and mode of delivery (definitive treatment) at a unit with neonatal support; transfer if required
Escalate to consultant obstetrician/MFM; document maternal and fetal monitoring plan

critical_errors: Failing to treat severe-range hypertension (BP greater than or equal to 160/110) — untreated severe BP risks maternal stroke
Not giving magnesium sulfate for seizure prophylaxis in severe pre-eclampsia with neurological signs (imminent eclampsia)
Withholding the diagnosis of pre-eclampsia because proteinuria is absent or not yet confirmed — proteinuria is NOT required when there is new hypertension plus end-organ dysfunction
Discharging or under-triaging the patient rather than admitting for stabilisation and delivery planning
must_not_miss: Severe hypertension treated promptly with a recognised agent (labetalol/nifedipine/hydralazine)
Magnesium sulfate given for eclampsia prophylaxis
HELLP syndrome and abruption considered; fetal wellbeing assessed with CTG
Definitive management (delivery) and senior obstetric escalation arranged
